title: Tinea Nomenclature by Body Site
description: Flip each card to match the body site to the correct tinea name and its key clinical feature.

dialogs.text: Fungal infection of the body trunk and limbs
dialogs.answer: Tinea corporis — annular lesions with a raised, scaly, advancing margin and relative central clearing; in India, often modified by steroid misuse into broad, ill-defined plaques

dialogs.text: Fungal infection of the groin and inner thighs
dialogs.answer: Tinea cruris — active scaly margin extending onto the medial thighs; characteristically spares the scrotum (scrotal involvement suggests Candida instead)
Tinea pedis — three patterns: interdigital (maceration between toes), vesicular (inflammatory blisters), or moccasin (dry hyperkeratotic scaling of the sole)

dialogs.text: Fungal infection of the scalp with hair involvement
dialogs.answer: Tinea capitis — requires systemic therapy (oral griseofulvin or terbinafine) because topical agents cannot penetrate the infected hair shaft; untreated, risks scarring alopecia
Tinea unguium (onychomycosis) — distal subungual dystrophy with discolouration and thickening; also requires systemic therapy for cure due to poor topical penetration of the nail plate
